# SaveShot

> Private screenshots straight to Google Drive or your computer.

SaveShot is a privacy-first, lightweight Chrome extension for capturing, highlighting, annotating, redacting, copying, and downloading screenshots locally right away with no sign-in required, or autosaving straight to your Google Drive with instant share links. Everything runs in Chrome with no external servers, no tracking, and no external dependencies.

## Key Capabilities

- **Capture options**: Select a screen area with pixel-exact HiDPI and zoom cropping, press `Enter` inside the selector for the full tab, capture the visible tab in one click, right-click any webpage and choose **Take Screenshot**, or set custom keyboard shortcuts at `chrome://extensions/shortcuts`.
- **Built-in screenshot editor**: Add arrows, rectangles, circles, lines, translucent marker highlights (`H`, hold `Shift` for a straight line), freehand pencil strokes, legible text callouts, custom `#HEX` colors, or solid black pixel redactions, plus rotate 90 degrees, flip, undo, or reset.
- **Instant clipboard and local export (no sign-in required)**: Click **Copy image** (or press `Ctrl+C` / `Cmd+C`) in the editor to copy a lossless PNG straight to your clipboard for pasting into AI assistants, chat apps, docs, or bug trackers, or click **Download** to save the PNG to your computer.
- **Direct Google Drive autosave**: Optionally connect Google Drive once to upload screenshots straight from Chrome into `Chrome_SaveShot_ScreenShots` (customizable in Settings) and copy the share link automatically, with a local PNG fallback if Drive is offline or full.

## Privacy and Security

- **No external servers**: Screenshots stay in Chrome or upload over HTTPS directly from the browser to Google's official Drive API (`https://www.googleapis.com`). SaveShot operates zero private, middleman, or analytics servers.
- **Narrow permissions**: Uses `activeTab` and `contextMenus` for user-triggered capture, and Google's narrow `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.file` scope when connected so SaveShot can only access the screenshots and folder it creates itself.
- **Incognito isolation**: When allowed in Incognito, SaveShot omits page URLs from filenames and Drive descriptions and skips local device history.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Do I need to sign in to capture and download screenshots?

No. You can capture an area or visible tab, highlight, annotate, or redact it in the editor, and click **Copy image** or **Download** with no sign-in required. Connect Google Drive whenever you want automatic cloud backup and instant share links.

### Does SaveShot use any external servers or track my data?

No. SaveShot runs in Chrome and uploads directly to Google Drive's official API. There are no SaveShot servers, no analytics, and no tracking. With Google's narrow `drive.file` scope, it cannot see any other files in your Drive.

### Can I redact sensitive details before uploading to Google Drive?

Yes. When signed in, screenshots upload right away by default so your share link is ready immediately. If you prefer to redact before anything is uploaded, turn on **Open editor before uploading** in Settings (or capture while signed out).

### How do keyboard shortcuts work?

SaveShot supports customizable shortcuts for both **Select area** and **Visible tab**. If a shortcut is not active because another extension already uses those keys, you can set your preferred keys anytime at `chrome://extensions/shortcuts` (or right-click any webpage and choose **Take Screenshot**).

### Why are capture buttons disabled on some tabs?

Chrome blocks all extensions from running on internal pages like `chrome://settings` and on the Chrome Web Store. For local PDFs or `file://` pages, turn on **Allow access to file URLs** in SaveShot's details at `chrome://extensions`.

### What happens if my Google Drive is full or offline?

If an upload fails after taking a screenshot, SaveShot shows a **Save PNG locally** button so you can save the image to your computer without losing it.

### How does Incognito mode work?

If you turn on **Allow in Incognito** in `chrome://extensions`, screenshots can still upload directly to your Google Drive while page URLs are left out of filenames and descriptions, and local upload history is skipped for privacy.
